title: Overriding & Dynamic Dispatch
hints: A subclass replaces a parent method with `override`; the object's real type decides which runs.
Each subclass overrides `summary()`; the manager's version calls `super.summary()`.
`override func summary() -> String { "I schedule meetings for \(hours) hours, then " + super.summary() }`.
jsBridge: Overriding works like JS classes (`class Developer extends Employee`), and the call goes to the runtime type (dynamic dispatch). Swift requires the `override` keyword, and `final` turns dispatch static. JS has neither.

compass.q: JS prototypes dispatch dynamically always. What does Swift's `final` buy (performance, intent), and why do Swift style guides mark classes `final` by default?
Java methods are virtual by default and `@Override` is optional. Why did Swift make `override` mandatory?
Class inheritance vs protocol with default implementations: which does Swift prefer for sharing behaviour?
UIKit subclassing (`UIViewController`) is everywhere. Why does SwiftUI avoid inheritance entirely?
